transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess I came in because my husband and the people down at the warehouse keep acting like I'm crazy. But I'm not. I know for a fact they’ve been watching my every move and going in and changing my pallet counts to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. It’s so obvious. 

And you know, speaking of pallets, you wouldn't believe how cheap the wood is getting these days. Half of them are splintered before we even load the freight on 'em. I got this massive splinter last Tuesday right through my heavy work glove. I had to dig it out with a safety pin in the breakroom. The breakroom vending machine is always out of Diet Coke, too, which really ticks me off because I need the caffeine when we're moving heavy stock all day. My husband drinks Mountain Dew, but I told him that stuff just rots your teeth out. He never listens to me though. But yeah, anyway, they all think I'm the crazy one just because I figured out they're messing with my numbers on the floor.
Do you ever hear voices when no one else is around?

Well, yeah, I guess so. Sometimes when I'm down in the aisle at the warehouse, or even just at home folding clothes, I'll hear this man's voice clear as day. He just says, "Nicole, check it again," even when there is absolutely nobody near me. 

But honestly, speaking of folding clothes, I am so sick of doing my husband's laundry. He leaves all these greasy receipts and wrappers in his pockets, and last week a whole wad of them went through the wash and got stuck to my good black work pants. I had to sit on the couch with a lint roller for twenty minutes just picking at the paper. And those lint rollers with the tear-off sheets are getting so expensive now! I started buying the generic ones down at the dollar store, but the tape on them barely sticks to anything. You really get what you pay for, I guess. I told him if he doesn't empty his pockets I'm throwing his jeans in the trash. But yeah, that guy's voice just tells me to check things when I'm by myself.
Have you had a period where you felt extremely depressed or unusually high or energized for days at a time?

Well, yeah, I definitely get like that. Some days I wake up and I am just fired up, you know? Like nobody can slow me down, I have all this energy and I'm ready to just go, go, go. But then if my husband asks me even one small question, like about the kids or my work schedule, I just snap at him. It feels like he's trying to control me or something. 

But honestly, speaking of my schedule, they keep messing with my shifts down at the warehouse. Last week they had me on the early morning load-in, which means I have to be there by 4:30 AM. Do you know how hard it is to scrape ice off your windshield at 4:00 in the morning? The scraper I have is one of those cheap plastic ones, and the edge is all chipped so it leaves these streaks of frost right in my line of sight. I meant to buy a new one with the brush on the other end, but the auto parts store is always closed by the time I get off my shift. And the guy who works the register there is always so slow anyway, like he’s got nowhere to be. But yeah, I get really energized sometimes and then just snap if my husband asks me anything.
Have the voice and the feeling that people are watching or sabotaging you ever happened during a time when your mood felt normal?

Yeah, actually. Even a few weeks ago, things were... quieter, I guess. I was sleeping okay, not racing around like a maniac like I do sometimes. But I still heard him. That guy's voice, just telling me to check things. And I still knew they were messing with my pallet counts, even when I felt totally fine. 

But you know, speaking of checking things, I had to check my tires like three times yesterday because the pressure light kept coming on in my Honda. I swear, that car is just falling apart. The front passenger tire has this slow leak, and I keep having to stop at the gas station on the corner of Elm to fill it up. And their air machine is a total rip-off! It used to be four quarters, now it’s two dollars, and it only takes cards half the time. The card reader is always sticky, like somebody spilled a slushie on it. I told my husband to just take the tire off and patch it, but he says he doesn't have the right jack for it. He’s got a whole garage full of tools he never uses. Just boxes of wrenches and sockets gathering dust while I'm out here spending two bucks a day on air. But yeah, even when my mood is normal, I still hear the voice and know they're sabotaging me at the warehouse.
About how long have you been hearing that man’s voice?

Well, let's see... the voices and that feeling that people are watching me or changing my things around, that's been going on for about eight months now. Yeah, eight months, because it started right when it was getting really hot last summer. 

And honestly, speaking of the heat, you would not believe how miserable it gets in that warehouse. They have these giant metal floor fans, but all they do is blow hot, dusty air right in your face. And the noise! It's like a jet engine running all shift. I asked the floor manager, Craig, if we could get some better ventilation, but he just brushed me off. Craig is always eating those barbecue sunflower seeds and spitting the shells into a styrofoam cup while he talks to you. It is so gross. Like, at least use a trash can, you know? He leaves those cups sitting on the breakroom tables, too, which just attracts ants. And then I go home and my husband keeps cranking our window AC unit down to 60 degrees, and our electric bill last month was absolutely through the roof. I told him we can't afford a bill like that, but he just ignores me. But yeah, it's been about eight months for the voice and all that.
Have these problems been going on for at least six months?

Well, yeah, like I said, it's been going on for about 10 months now. It all really started getting bad when the arguments at home got worse, right after I started trying to get that shift-supervisor role at the warehouse. 

Which, by the way, is a total joke of a process. They make you take this online test on these ancient computers in the back office. The keyboards are all sticky, and half the keys have the letters rubbed off, so you have to guess if you're hitting an 'E' or an 'R'. And the chair! It's one of those cheap office chairs where the hydraulic lift is broken, so every time you sit down, you just sink all the way to the floor. I felt like a little kid sitting at the grown-up table. And Craig—remember Craig with his gross sunflower seeds?—he was supposed to be proctoring the test, but he just sat in the corner on his phone the whole time, probably playing Candy Crush or whatever. I don't even know why I bother trying to move up when management doesn't even care. But yeah, it's been about 10 months since all this started.
During these 10 months, have the times when you felt unusually energized or depressed lasted for most of that period?

Yeah, definitely. If I look at this whole stretch, for more than half of it, easily, I've had these really fired-up periods. I barely sleep at all, I take on way too many projects, and I get so irritable if anyone tries to get in my way or slow me down. 

Like, speaking of taking on too much, I decided a while back I was going to completely reorganize that garage I was telling you about, because my husband's tool situation was just a disaster. I went to Target to buy all these plastic bins—the heavy-duty clear ones with the blue latch handles? They were actually on sale, buy two get one free, which is a pretty good deal, but the checkout line was backed up all the way into the women's clothing section. And the cashier was moving so slow, I swear she was reading the numbers on every single barcode before she scanned it. The lady in front of me was buying like forty little glass jars of baby food, and I almost just left my cart right there and walked out because I couldn't handle the waiting. But I brought the bins home and stayed up for like three days straight just sorting wrenches and sockets by size. My husband told me to just leave it and come to bed, and I absolutely lost it on him for trying to stop me. But yeah, those energized stretches have definitely lasted for the majority of the ten months.
